events.title: Praetorians murder Pertinax and auction the empire
events.description: After killing Emperor Pertinax, the Praetorian Guard sold the throne to the senator Didius Julianus, who outbid his rival. He lasted 66 days before Septimius Severus took power.
events.html: After killing Emperor Pertinax, the Praetorian Guard sold the throne to the senator Didius Julianus, who outbid his rival. He lasted 66 days before Septimius Severus took power.

events.title: Valentinian I makes his brother Valens co-emperor
events.description: At Constantinople, the Roman emperor Valentinian I made his brother Valens co-Augustus, giving him the eastern half of the empire and keeping the West for himself. Valens ruled until 378, when he was killed fighting the Goths at Adrianople.

events.title: Confederate Ireland signs the First Ormond Peace with Charles I
events.description: For the Supreme Council of Confederate Ireland, Donough MacCarty signed the First Ormond Peace with Ormonde for King Charles I, in exchange for greater freedom of religion. It was signed unbeknownst to the Confederate commanders and without the papal nuncio, Rinuccini.

events.title: Austria defeats France at the Battle of Vilshofen
events.description: In the War of the Austrian Succession, Austrian forces defeated the French and then plundered Vilshofen. The war was fought over Maria Theresa's right to inherit the Habsburg lands after the death of Emperor Charles VI.
events.html: In the War of the Austrian Succession, Austrian forces defeated the French and then plundered Vilshofen. The war was fought over Maria Theresa's right to inherit the Habsburg lands after the death of Emperor Charles VI.

events.title: British warships capture USS Essex off Valparaíso
events.description: Off Valparaíso, Chile, the frigate HMS Phoebe and the sloop HMS Cherub fought the frigate USS Essex and the sloop USS Essex Junior. The British ships won, and both American vessels were captured.

events.title: Britain and France declare war on Russia
events.description: The two powers joined the Ottoman Empire against Russia, beginning their part in the Crimean War. Battlefield reporting and Florence Nightingale's nursing made it a turning point in public views of war.
events.html: The two powers joined the Ottoman Empire against Russia, beginning their part in the Crimean War. Battlefield reporting and Florence Nightingale's nursing made it a turning point in public views of war.

events.title: Henri Fabre makes the first seaplane flight
events.description: The French engineer took off from the Étang de Berre near Marseille in his float-equipped Hydravion. It was the first powered aircraft to take off from water.
events.html: The French engineer took off from the Étang de Berre near Marseille in his float-equipped Hydravion. It was the first powered aircraft to take off from water.

events.title: Virginia Woolf drowns herself in the River Ouse
events.description: Fearing a return of mental illness, the novelist filled her pockets with stones and walked into the river near her Sussex home. Her novels include 'Mrs Dalloway' and 'To the Lighthouse'.
events.html: Fearing a return of mental illness, the novelist filled her pockets with stones and walked into the river near her Sussex home. Her novels include 'Mrs Dalloway' and 'To the Lighthouse'.

events.title: Partial meltdown at Three Mile Island
events.description: A cooling failure caused part of a reactor core to melt at the Pennsylvania nuclear plant. Little radiation escaped, but it was the worst US nuclear accident and stalled new reactor orders.

song: Catholic Germany, where the Latin hymn was first printed; later the Church of England and English-speaking churches
